title: Day, Night & Our Calendar
source: Science G3 B1 Study sheet pp.44-47, Worksheet Day and Night Investigation

scenes.t: The Earth spins around an imaginary line called its axis. This spinning is called rotation. One full spin takes 24 hours, which is one day.
The side of the Earth facing the Sun has day. The side facing away from the Sun has night.
The Earth also travels around the Sun. This is called revolution, or orbit. One full trip takes 365 and a quarter days, which is one year.
The Moon orbits the Earth about every 28 days. This makes one lunar month.
The Gregorian calendar follows the Earth's trip around the Sun. It has 12 months of 30 or 31 days, but February has 28 days.
Every year has an extra quarter of a day. So every four years we add one day to February, giving it 29 days. That year has 366 days and is called a leap year.
The Islamic calendar also has 12 months. Each month starts when people see the crescent moon, called the Hilal, so a month has 29 or 30 days.

items.a: The Earth spinning on its axis. Takes 24 hours = 1 day.
The Earth orbiting the Sun. Takes 365¼ days = 1 year.
The imaginary line the Earth spins around.
The Moon orbits the Earth in about 28 days.
A year with 366 days. It comes every 4 years.
Seeing it starts a new Islamic month.
28 days, or 29 in a leap year.

activities.title: Day and Night Model
activities.goal: Show how the Earth's spin makes day and night.

predict.q: When your sticker faces the lamp, is it day or night there?

steps.t: Turn on the lamp and switch off the room lights. The lamp is the Sun.
Put a sticker on the ball. This is where you live.
Hold the ball near the lamp and spin it slowly.
Watch the sticker: when it faces the lamp it is in light, when it turns away it is in the dark.

activities.result: When the sticker faces the lamp it is day there. When it turns away, it is night.
activities.why: The Earth's rotation on its axis every 24 hours causes day and night.
